inputs.proposal: Bridge cleanup after the coalescing change: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer, signal decode reads the standard 8-byte CAN payload, the staging buffer is rebuilt per frame, and dropped frames are reported from the GUI-side frame handler.
inputs.original_proposal: Bridge cleanup after the coalescing change: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer, signal decode reads the standard 8-byte CAN payload, the staging buffer is rebuilt per frame, and dropped frames are reported from the GUI-side frame handler.

blockers:
claim: Staging buffer is cleared on every frame, eliminating the intended merge of latest values per signal ID across frames within the coalescing window, thus changing the semantics of signal updates.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: m_stagingBuffer.clear();
for (uint32_t i = 0; i < set->count; ++i) {
questions: Is it acceptable that frame count and dropped frame count are only updated when handleFrameInternal runs, potentially undercounting frames received during backpressure?
Will the hardcoded 8‑byte payload length in qttune_decode_signal be compatible with all supported CAN and CAN‑FD frames, or should it use the actual frame data length?
Does the removal of notifyDropped() and the drop notification logic meet the required error propagation and user feedback requirements?
Is the missing clamp on frame->data_length a deliberate design choice for performance, or an oversight that could lead to out‑of‑bounds reads?

claim: Signal decoding uses a hardcoded payload length of 8 bytes instead of the actual frame length, which can produce incorrect decoding for non-8‑byte frames and may read past the payload buffer.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: if (qttune_decode_signal(&def, frame->data, 8, &val) == 0) {
nits: Consider adding a comment explaining why the hardcoded 8‑byte payload length is used or removing the hardcoded value.
Remove the unused member variable m_lastReportedDropped to keep the code clean.
The setSignalSet() parameter could be renamed to maintain clarity about its opaque nature (e.g., const void* opaqueSet).
